title: Arm the scheduler-to-crier dispatch leg (built, never run)
reasoning: internal/bus/dispatch.go + dispatch_leg.go + slot_pool.go:729 already implement dispatch through crier, with a tick_dispatch receipt table. It has never run: CRIER_AGENT_ID and CRIER_AGENT_KEY_FILE are unset so InboxEnabled() is false; no dispatch-targets.jsonl row declares a remote lane; the scheduler is not registered on the relay so replies 404. The payload also lacks a text member, so the receiving dispatcher runs the raw JSON as a prompt.
acceptance_criteria: 1. WorkItem payload carries text; internal/bus/dispatch_test.go and docs/dispatch-spec.md pin the wire shape. 2. The relay Hermes template and dispatcher.py both consume the same member, proven by a test. 3. A dry-run renders a directive, not a JSON blob. 4. Removing the target row returns the lane to the local path, proven by a second tick. 7. Arming done on a branch/worktree with tests, never by editing the live daemon in place.

title: Node inference credential: restricted inference key, fail-closed on revoke
reasoning: Hermes runs in a bunker and its gateway answers over the tailnet, but a turn dies at 'agent init failed: No inference provider configured'. The inference gateway is reachable from a node, while the routing proxy and resolve API bind loopback only. The sanctioned pattern is a revocable restricted key (accessRestricted + accessAllow, enforced before credential lookup), never an operator key on a remote box.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A restricted key allows only the models a node needs; a test proves every other model/route is refused. 2. The node's ~/.hermes/.env carries it, mode 600, never in argv or a log. 3. prompt.submit through the node gateway returns a completion, with requested vs served model recorded. 4. Revoking the key fails closed with a readable error, proven live. 5. No operator credential is copied to any agent; blast radius stated in specs/HARNESS.md.

title: Per-repo deploy key + node runtime + shared module cache
reasoning: Measured: a public repo clones and builds in a node (3.6 s clone, 105 s cold build, suite 30/30 with node present) but a private GitLab needs auth the agent does not have (:22 publickey denied, :2222/:3030 refused; the control host only works via an insteadOf rewrite). go test -short fails 11 tests with exec node not found, so a green without node is wrong. Every node re-downloads a 656 MB module cache (~1.5 GB footprint) on a host at 92-98%.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A read-only per-repo deploy key is injected at spawn; cloning the private GitLab from a fresh node succeeds in one documented command. 2. The repo's test runtime (node for several Go repos) is present and the 11 node-dependent tests pass; suite 30/30 from a clean node. 3. A shared read-only GOMODCACHE removes the 656 MB re-download and the improvement is measured. 4. Per-node footprint measured against the disk floor. 5. Orphan homes/keys reaped to zero.

title: Round trip through the node's own gateway (not a bespoke poller)
reasoning: MDP-1 proved dispatch/execute/verify with a python worker written for the occasion. The target architecture puts the work into a harness behind the node's gateway. Until a directive travels crier -> node -> Hermes gateway -> result, the factory is still relaying through a script we wrote.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A directive is pushed to the node's crier inbox and reaches the Hermes gateway (session.create + prompt.submit), with the crier message id and the gateway session id both recorded. 2. The result returns over crier with a correlated dispatch id and the node's hostname. 3. A commit produced in the node is visible from the control host with the same sha. 4. An artifact digest is recomputed on the control host and matches. 5. A negative control (gateway stopped, or gate made to fail) produces a recorded FAIL, not a silent success.

title: Node specs + design + installer scripts (this repo)
reasoning: The factory needs an authority for what a node is and how one is made, so the ladder stops living in chat transcripts and ad-hoc commands.
acceptance_criteria: 1. specs/NODE.md, specs/ENVELOPE.md, specs/HARNESS.md and docs/DESIGN.md exist and agree with the scripts. 2. scripts/project-node.sh --check runs inside a node and can FAIL (selftest proves it). 3. scripts/node-create.sh creates a node from a project+repo+harness triple. 4. scripts/verify-node.sh checks reachability, the auth gate, and an artifact digest. 5. tests/selftest.sh is green on a clean tree and red on a broken one.

title: Foreign harness adapters: opencode, claude-code, codex, aider, goose, pi-agent
reasoning: The factory must not assume Hermes. crier's examples already run six CLI harnesses behind one bus, but none of them has a measured install ladder inside a bunker, and node is absent from the base image (claude-code cannot install without it). An unverified installer must say so out loud rather than pretend support.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Each adapter has --check (real) and --apply (refused until measured). 2. At least one foreign harness is measured end to end in a node and its ladder recorded in specs/HARNESS.md. 3. That harness answers a directive non-interactively and returns a machine-readable result. 4. A node created with that harness passes verify-node.sh. 5. The node manifest records the harness name and version.

title: Node sizing and disk policy: refuse admission with the number
reasoning: Measured: 4.3 GB free inside an agent on a host at 97%, while one repo node costs ~1.5 GB and sibling agents swing free space by 5 GB. Without a policy nodes fill the host and fail mid-job, which is the orphaned-work failure this fleet has already had.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A documented floor per node role, justified by measured footprint. 2. The ladder refuses admission below the floor, naming the number, before any install begins. 3. A reclaim step (build cache, job dirs, stale clones) runs before refusal. 4. A boundary test proves the refusal fires. 5. bunker status residue (orphan homes/keys/users) is reaped and reported.

title: Node lifecycle: supervisor, renew, destroy/rebuild
reasoning: A node's gateway is started with nohup and dies on agent stop/renew; agent TTL is 4h unless renewed. A node that silently disappears is indistinguishable from a node that failed, and cancellation is only possible by killing the process group from a second exec (client kill and --timeout do NOT stop remote work).
acceptance_criteria: 1. The harness runs under a supervisor that restarts it and records restarts. 2. Agent TTL is renewed automatically while the node is active. 3. Cancelling a dispatch kills the process GROUP and the evidence shows it (job pid/pgid written by the job, killed, completion artifact absent after the deadline). 4. destroy then create reproduces the node from recorded commands with no manual step. 5. A node that dies mid-job causes redelivery, and idempotency prevents duplicated work.
